subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Out of every hospital in Rhode Island on Medicare's list, every kind counted.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Newport Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Lifespan hospitals; Rhode Island Hospital has the most, 7,076. About 10.5 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Rhode Island Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: No other Lifespan hospital reports more; The Miriam Hospital is next at 2,614. About 10.9 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did The Miriam Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Lifespan hospitals; Rhode Island Hospital has the most, 7,076. About 10.6 for every bed.

questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Lifespan's hospitals have on payroll, added together?

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians train in Lifespan's hospitals, added together?
questions.why: 2 of its hospitals report residents; Rhode Island Hospital trains the most, 494.

questions.q: What percent of Newport Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Lifespan hospitals; The Miriam Hospital runs highest, 70 percent. Traditional Medicare was 31 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 32 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Rhode Island Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 Lifespan hospitals; The Miriam Hospital runs highest, 70 percent. Traditional Medicare was 19 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 32 percent.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Lifespan run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in Rhode Island. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: What percent of the hospitals in Rhode Island belong to Lifespan?
questions.why: 4 of 13. The next biggest system there, Care New England Health System, has 3.
